diagnostic:
P1-P5, T1 and the content-hash migration are implemented and the new oracle is green, but one shipped law goes red for a reason no implementation can remove, so this batch is not complete.

GREEN, on one consistent tree: cargo xtask smoke printed "xtask smoke :: all gates green" (exit 0, fmt + clippy + check-arch + workspace release tests); ui-nav-polish 26 scenarios, 26 passed, 170 steps; nav-quick-actions 9/9; nav-collapse-icon-rail 17/17; instance-admin-workspace-rename (iawr) 27/27; cargo test -p foundry-app nav exit 0 with the totality test extended over all five variants; check-arch green including the new mark-carrier rule.

BLOCKED BY DESIGN. canzan-theme-system is 26 of 28, 2 failed: "every large-text and control-boundary pair reaches at least 3 to 1" and "the same holds when the device preference is light". Both panic with: dark palette: `button.sidebar__item[Sign out]` computes only 0.00:1 () against #0f1312 - nothing identifies this control at WCAG 1.4.11's 3:1 (and the light twin against #f3f4f1). That shipped walk reads EVERY visible button inside .app-shell and demands that the better of its own OPAQUE fill and its border reach 3:1 against the surface behind it; a transparent fill is skipped and a zero-width border counts as none. P5, as oracled, demands of the sign-out submit and of the theme control: the same painted fill as the rail surface, a border no wider than the neighbour links' (zero), and the neighbours' colour and weight. Fill equal to the surface computes 1:1, transparent is skipped, and no border is allowed, so no implementation satisfies both laws for those two buttons; no third property (outline, shadow) is read by the shipped walk. The theme control has no escape at all: its fill must equal the very surface it is measured against.

OWNER: design. The Impact table declares canzan-theme-system UnchangedCompatible, and the quiet-lower-group decision argues the 1.4.11 border may go "because the control becomes text-plus-glyph like its neighbours" - but the shipped law enumerates BUTTONS, not controls-that-need-identifying, so the argument does not reach the checker. REMEDY, architect's choice: keep an identifying property on those two controls and ask the acceptance designer to adjust the P5 comparison; or request the acceptance designer migrate the 1.4.11 scope for rail members drawn as text-plus-glyph (the same migration this oracle already performed for nav-quick-actions and the icon rail); or take it back to product. I changed no oracle byte.

MECHANISM NOTE on P4. The decision says the workspace name "leaves the layout exactly as it already does when the rail is folded", i.e. display: none. That red the shipped iawr phone row "the sidebar shows the workspace name on one line ending in an ellipsis" (scrollWidth 0 <= clientWidth 0) - a lane the Impact table does not list. The name is therefore CLIPPED out of the flow instead (position: absolute, 1px, clip-path: inset(50%), text-overflow and overflow untouched), which is the mechanism this same design blesses for a member's word and for the same reason: the element stays in the document for the promise that reads it. The bar still measures two rows and all four phone rows pass.

REFACTOR (design-ordered prefactoring, L1 to L2): crates/foundry-app/src/admin_tokens.rs - the four renders at the index, the issuing-not-enabled notice, the minted-value page and the validation re-render each assembled the rail with the same five arguments; they now call one private nav_for, so the section this module marks is named ONCE. It is NOT a commit of its own: nwdes commit refuses before a close receipt (MissingCloseReceipt), and the follow-up edit that names tokens_for lives in the same file, so the extraction could not be published ahead of the behaviour change.

ALL-LANE READING, honestly: FOUNDRY_ACCEPTANCE_TAGS=all reported 2313 scenarios, 68 failed. 2 are the theme rows above and 1 was the iawr row now fixed. The other 65 are an artefact of MY OWN rsync: scripts/test-in-lima.sh copied the re-hashed stylesheet into the VM while that suite was still running, so its pages were served with no CSS at all ("the open rail is 1249.0px wide instead of the 240px it ships with"). The five lanes re-run afterwards on one consistent tree show only the 2 theme rows red. The whole suite has NOT been re-run clean since; that is unmeasured.
